DEFINE.core_strategy: Extend the existing single-invocation report so every successful run also states the file's line count, appended to the same stdout line. The line rule is defined once, Unicode-aware and independent of the word and character rules, and is kept as pure counting logic separate from the command shell, as the existing counters are. The change is purely additive: invocation, word and character results, UTF-8 handling and every error path behave exactly as they do today, so the only visible difference for users is one extra field on success.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Make the line count opt-in behind a new flag or option
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: Contradicts the approved Problem Graph and handoff, which require no new flag. It also changes the invocation surface that SPEC-0002 guards and leaves the default output without the count users asked for.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Adopt the narrower POSIX wc -l convention of counting only LF line feeds
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: Familiar, but the human explicitly chose a broader rule. Files with lone CR, U+2028 or form feed would report counts that disagree with the agreed definition and its tests.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Count line segments, including an unterminated final segment
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: Matches some editors' intuition, but conflicts with the confirmed example that 'a\nb' reports 1. It also makes an unterminated single-line file report 1 where the agreed rule reports 0, which reopens a settled boundary.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Fold line counting into the existing word or character counting responsibility
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: Adds no new unit, but blurs the architecture boundary in which each counter owns exactly one rule. It also risks regressions in the word and character results that SPEC-0001 and SPEC-0002 guard.

rejected_alternatives.direction: Report the line count on a separate stdout line or in a separate command
rejected_alternatives.tradeoff: Leaves the existing line untouched, but breaks the agreed single-line `words: <N> characters: <M> lines: <L>` format. Users would also lose the one-invocation, one-line report that is the point of the change.

assumptions.description: Users and any scripts consuming the output accept a format change on the success line, as they did when SPEC-0002 replaced the bare integer
assumptions.how_checked: Owner confirmation during strategy and spec review, and the README is updated to state the new line format
assumptions.if_false: Return to DISCOVER to weigh output compatibility against the always-on requirement

assumptions.description: The Python standard library's own line-boundary definition is stable across the supported Python versions, so the agreed rule yields the same counts everywhere the project runs
assumptions.how_checked: Acceptance examples covering LF, CRLF, lone CR, U+2028, form feed, whitespace-only and unterminated-final-segment files pass under the Quality Gate
assumptions.if_false: Define the terminator set explicitly in the spec instead of by reference to the library behaviour

assumptions.description: The line count can be derived from the same decoded text already used for words and characters, so no new reading or decoding path is needed
assumptions.how_checked: Review that error-path guardrail tests (missing, unreadable, invalid UTF-8) still pass unchanged and print nothing to stdout
assumptions.if_false: Revisit the scope with the owner before touching error handling

risks.description: The broad terminator set surprises users who expect wc -l results, for example on files containing form feeds or lone CRs
risks.impact: Perceived incorrect counts and bug reports
risks.mitigation: Document the rule and its difference from wc -l in the README, with the confirmed examples

risks.description: Changing the success line breaks existing tests and downstream consumers that match `words: <N> characters: <M>` exactly
risks.impact: Failing existing CLI and feature tests, and broken user scripts
risks.mitigation: Update affected tests deliberately in the spec, and state the format change in the README as SPEC-0002 did

risks.description: Wiring in a new count accidentally alters word or character results, or error-path behaviour
risks.mitigation: Carry the SPEC-0002 regression guardrails forward unchanged, and require all four Quality Gate commands to pass

risks.description: The CRLF single-terminator case or the unterminated-final-segment case is implemented inconsistently
risks.impact: Off-by-one line counts on Windows-origin or unterminated files
risks.mitigation:

DEFINE.thesis: Complete the wordcount report by always appending a clearly defined, Unicode-aware line count to the existing success line, now that users have asked for it and the boundary rule is settled, without disturbing anything already built.

goals.description: Users get the line count of a file from the same single `wordcount PATH` invocation that already reports words and characters
goals.why: Removes the need for a separate tool, which is the core issue in DG-0003
goals.success_metric: 100% of successful runs print a `lines: <L>` field on the single stdout line

goals.description: Line counts are unambiguous and agree with the agreed boundary rule on every file shape
goals.why: DG-0003 rates an ambiguous rule as high severity for correctness
goals.success_metric: All DG-0003 boundary examples (LF, CRLF, lone CR, U+2028, form feed, whitespace-only, unterminated final segment, empty) report the agreed counts

goals.description: Existing behaviour stays intact: invocation, word and character results, UTF-8 handling and error paths
goals.why: The handoff and the SPEC-0001/0002 guardrails require it
goals.success_metric: 0 regressions across the existing guardrail tests, and all four Quality Gate commands exit 0

success_criteria.criterion: Success output includes the line count
success_criteria.measurement: CLI acceptance tests on stdout of `wordcount PATH`
success_criteria.target: Exactly one line `words: <N> characters: <M> lines: <L>` on every successful run

'a
b' gives 1; '

' gives 2 (with 0 words and 0 characters); 'a
' gives 1; empty file gives 0; lone CR, U+2028 and form feed each count as a terminator
100% pass; error paths still print nothing to stdout, and exit statuses 1 and 2 are unchanged

success_criteria.measurement: ruff format check, ruff check, mypy --strict, pytest

non_goals.description: Making the line count optional or configurable
non_goals.tradeoff: Keeps the invocation unchanged and simple, at the cost of no way to get the old two-field output
The agreed Unicode-aware rule is clearer for mixed-platform text, at the cost of differing from a familiar tool on some files

non_goals.description: Other statistics (bytes, longest line, per-line output) or stdin or batch input
non_goals.tradeoff: Keeps scope small, consistent with the architecture's stated non-ownership; those requests wait for their own discovery

non_goals.description: Preserving byte-for-byte compatibility of the previous success line
non_goals.tradeoff: Delivers the requested one-line report, at the cost of breaking consumers of the old format

in_scope: Always appending ` lines: <L>` to the existing success stdout line
A single line-counting rule: every boundary the standard library line-splitting recognises terminates a line, CRLF counts once, and an unterminated final segment is not counted
Line counting as pure logic with no I/O, beside the existing word and character rules
README documentation of the new output line and the line rule, including how it differs from wc -l
Updating existing tests that assert the old two-field line
out_of_scope: New flags, options or changes to the single positional PATH invocation
Any change to the word rule (word-counter) or the character rule (character-counter)
Any change to UTF-8 decoding, error messages, exit statuses or argparse usage behaviour
stdin, multiple files, non-UTF-8 encodings or other statistics

walkthrough.name: Ordinary multi-line file
today: User runs a separate tool to learn the file has 2 lines

walkthrough.name: Unterminated final line and CRLF
today: File 'a\nb' gives `words: 2 characters: 2`, with no line information
with_strategy: File 'a\nb' gives `words: 2 characters: 2 lines: 1`, because the trailing 'b' has no terminator
File 'a\r\n' gives `words: 1 characters: 1 lines: 1`, because CRLF is one break

walkthrough.name: Error paths unchanged
today: A missing file prints `wordcount: error: file not found: PATH` to stderr, nothing to stdout, and exits 1
with_strategy: Identical: same stderr line, nothing on stdout, exit 1, and no line count is ever printed on error

DISCOVER.Should the line count follow `wc -l` (co: Follow the terminated-line convention: a followed by LF followed by b reports 1; do not count an unterminated final segment. Use the broader separators specified below.
DISCOVER.What should a whitespace-only file such: 2 lines. The human explicitly confirmed this correction.
DISCOVER.Which line terminators count as line bre: Every boundary Python str.splitlines() recognizes, with CRLF counted once. The human confirmed combining broader separators with not counting an unterminated final line.
DISCOVER.Should the line count always be printed: Always print the line count, with no new flag, retaining the single-PATH invocation.
